## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Rocket League-style car soccer game where chosen cosmetic items alter car stats/physics.
- Current work: polishing visuals, camera behavior, and gameplay feel after implementing the full game.

## Requirements
- "3D Rocket League with different stats based off the 'cosmetics' used"
- This is a build request: deliver a complete playable game now, make reasonable assumptions, do not ask clarifying questions.
- Support mobile/touch and responsive layouts.

## Decisions
- Built with Three.js + Vite, single-page app, no external runtime assets except bundled local fonts.
- 1v1 car soccer vs AI with 3:00 regulation, overtime, boost pads, jump/double-jump, drift, ball cam, pause, rematch.
- Four cosmetic categories (`body`, `wheels`, `boost`, `topper`), each item applying stat modifiers that feed real physics values (max speed, acceleration, steering, grip, jump, hit power, boost capacity/thrust/regen).
- Custom 3D arena: procedural field texture, stands/crowd, neon goal nets, boost pads, truss lights, sky/stars/planet, bloom postprocessing, synthesized WebAudio.
- Visual style is stylized neon sci-fi rather than photoreal AAA.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold, Vite build, Three.js dependency, local Orbitron/Rajdhani fonts.
- `index.html`, full menu/garage/HUD/pause/end-modal/touch UI, responsive CSS.
- Cosmetics data and stat computation (`src/cosmetics.js`).
- Arena, goals, nets, boost pads, crowd, stands, lighting, sky/planet (`src/arena.js`).
- Car physics, AI support, car model/toppers/wheels/flames (`src/car.js`).
- Ball physics/visuals (`src/ball.js`), particles/rings/FX (`src/effects.js`), synthesized audio (`src/audio.js`).
- Main game loop/state machine/input/camera/HUD/garage wiring (`src/main.js`).
- Menu and match run successfully; screenshots verified; no console errors.
- Goal detection, goal cinematic/banner, AI scoring, boost, speed, HUD all observed working.
- Ball cam now clamps yaw so player car remains in view when ball is to the side.
- Menu camera framing places car clear of garage/hero panels; lighting/bloom tuned to reduce overexposure.
- `npm run build` passes.

### Active
- Reviewing latest gameplay screenshot (`screenshots/cam_side.png`) to assess camera framing, ball visibility, car visuals, and overall gameplay polish.
- Potential final polish: reduce ball wireframe shell prominence, improve car detail, verify mobile layout, test garage item switching and match end flow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/cam_side.png`; fix any camera/car visibility issues.
2. Reduce ball shell wireframe opacity/geometry (`src/ball.js`) if still too prominent.
3. Test garage tab/item selection rebuilds car and updates telemetry visually.
4. Test pause/resume, end-match modal, rematch/garage flow.
5. Test mobile viewport/touch controls and responsive menu.
6. Re-run `npm run build`, capture final menu/match screenshots, stop or leave dev server as appropriate.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game loop, state machine, camera, input, UI wiring, AI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/car.js`: car physics, ball collisions, car visual builder.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/arena.js`: arena/scene/lighting/goals/boost pads.
